tasks.short: Identify and implement solutions to information security problems.

steps.what: Diagnose the information security problem from affected assets and incident evidence
Evaluate security solutions against exposure, compatibility and service disruption
Prepare security configuration changes and rollback settings in the security management console
Test the proposed security solution and rollback against representative service traffic
Approve the exact tested security change, target assets and rollback
Apply the approved security solution through the security management console

tasks.design: Reuse tested policy objects in the security-management category of {OTHER}. The engineer diagnoses the problem and tests the exact proposed configuration and rollback before a version-bound deployment gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Similar remediation changes require repeated target selection and configuration entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native configuration profiles and deployment jobs can reuse mechanics without choosing security policy.
tasks.still_hard: A fix may block legitimate traffic or move the vulnerability elsewhere.
tasks.human_edge: Judge service consequences and whether the solution addresses the actual threat.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated configuration entry; risk acceptance remains with the existing authorized roles.

reach.task: Validate whether a remediation removes an exploit path

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: security-management consoles support reusable policy objects, staged changes and deployment jobs; applicability and rollout safety still require engineering judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is diagnosis through internal deployment of a configuration remedy, not procurement or a major application rewrite. Shares are provisional, not measured.

Existing incident and asset producers supply timestamps, affected asset IDs, relevant alerts, current policy revision and service dependencies. s1 checks gaps and manually investigates missing context; there is no assumed structured diagnosis.

s3 produces target IDs, exact setting diff, configuration version, test target, deployment window and rollback settings. Field reuse touches repeated values only; security-specific choices retain time.

Test native {OTHER} profiles first. No reduction is credited to test runtime or already automated configuration. Changed configurations return to testing and approval; deployment is denied on missing targets or stale approval. The engineer is assumed authorized for this bounded change.
research_questions: Do repeated configuration fields account for the proposed nine hours without reducing solution design or testing?

already_counted.description: Approve the final tested configuration and rollback

incremental.description: Maintain reusable profiles and deployment validation rules

approvals.approved_version: Exact configuration revision, target set, window and rollback approved in s5; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes nine repeated-entry hours and five deployment hours less two upkeep. Low assumes bespoke configuration throughout, with deployment mechanics alone changed. Diagnosis, solution choice and testing retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop information security standards and best practices.

steps.what: Examine applicable security guidance and current control failures
Choose security standards, exceptions and proportionate implementation requirements
Draft information security standards and practical implementation examples

loop.purpose: Express chosen controls as clear standards without adding obligations
loop.input: Engineer decisions and source extracts with document revisions
loop.output: Draft clauses with source references and flagged gaps
loop.check: Engineer compares every obligation, exception and example against decisions and tests whether examples actually satisfy the intended control
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved meaning or unsupported controls return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates supply headings, but varied control evidence must be translated into clear prose

steps.what: Approve the complete security standards revision for internal release
Publish the approved security standards revision in the controlled document store

tasks.design: Start with the native controlled-document template in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop expresses the engineer's control decisions; source-based semantic review precedes approval and publication of the complete revision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning varied guidance and implementation decisions into consistent prose is repeated work.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked drafting can propose language while document version controls govern release.
tasks.still_hard: A readable standard can be technically unsafe or impossible for a service owner to meet.
tasks.human_edge: Set proportionate requirements and distinguish enforceable controls from aspirations.
tasks.altitude: More time validating implementability; no new policy authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: constrained language drafting can express supplied control decisions, but semantic and technical review is required before policy publication.

assumptions: Boundary covers standards development and controlled internal publication. It excludes inventing controls from a model and the downstream implementation project. Shares are provisional.

s1 selects actual guidance revisions and records evidence extracts; s2 captures chosen requirement, scope, exception condition and rationale in its retained time. The loop does not receive unexplained machine-ready decisions.

Try native template and clause reuse first. The loop is only justified for variable explanatory prose; if clauses already exist, retain native reuse instead. s3 includes source mapping, corrections and meaning review; s4 checks the complete release.

The engineer is an authorized release approver for these technical standards; if separate management ratification is required, measure that outside-role work before rollout. Missing sources stop drafting rather than allowing fabricated obligations.
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce writing time without silently changing control scope or exceptions?

already_counted.description: Review draft meaning and correct control prose

incremental.description: Maintain source permissions, prompt examples and revision regression checks

approvals.approved_version: Complete standards document revision and internal release scope approved in s4; edits invalidate approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:10.5 drafting hours saved less three upkeep. Low: semantic correction consumes the drafting benefit. Same-library publication, requirements choice and final acceptance retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend information security enhancements to management.

steps.what: Assemble security findings, affected services and existing enhancement costs
Select recommended security enhancements and explain residual risk and delivery trade-offs
Prepare the management recommendation with supporting costs and security evidence
Approve the final management recommendation and recipient list
Send the approved security enhancement recommendation to management
Explain security enhancements to management and answer risk and investment questions

tasks.design: Use native saved exports from the security-monitoring category of {OTHER} and existing {PROCUREMENT} estimates. Reuse figures in a {DOCS} briefing, keep recommendation reasoning and management discussion human, and gate the exact internal send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefings repeat finding exports, service matching and copying supporting figures.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report filters and linked document tables can reuse existing evidence without generating a risk judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Security exposure and delivery cost are uncertain and competing priorities are legitimate.
tasks.human_edge: Make a defensible recommendation and engage management on consequences.
tasks.altitude: Less evidence assembly before management discussions; investment decisions remain with management.

reach.task: Estimate operational consequences of security changes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: saved security exports and linked briefing tables can reduce repeated gathering and figure copying without selecting the investment recommendation.

assumptions: Boundary includes written recommendation, delivery and focal-role management discussion. It does not include management deliberation or implementing the eventual investment. Shares are illustrative.

Security systems supply finding ID, asset ID, severity and timestamp; service inventory owners supply asset-to-service links; purchasing supplies estimate amount, currency, date and scope. s1 manually resolves missing links and stale estimates rather than assuming clean inputs.

s2 writes rationale; s3 saves only evidence copying and recurring layout. Native exports and linked tables are tested first, with manual assembly where unavailable. No artificial narrative generator or invented cost baseline is introduced.
The recipient list is selected and checked in s4. A changed recommendation or audience requires reapproval. The send is internal; it does not authorize expenditure.
research_questions: Which parts of briefing assembly are actually repeated copying rather than risk interpretation?

already_counted.description: Verify final recommendation, evidence and audience

incremental.description: Maintain saved export joins and briefing fields

approvals.approved_version: Final recommendation revision, attachments and management recipients approved in s4; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten evidence-gathering, four figure-copying and five dispatch hours less two upkeep. Low assumes evidence already integrated and narrative bespoke, leaving dispatch only. Reasoning and discussion retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Oversee risk assessments and security system tests.

steps.what: Define risk assessment scope and security system test acceptance criteria
Gather risk assessment evidence and test results from assessment repositories
Track test completion and unresolved assessment exceptions against the agreed scope
Challenge assessment conclusions and resolve security test exceptions with assessors
Draft the security assessment oversight closure and unresolved conditions
Approve the final oversight closure and remaining risk conditions
Record the approved risk assessment oversight closure in the project record

tasks.design: Configure scope-linked evidence views in {PROJECT} and the assessment-repository category of {OTHER}. Native status roll-ups expose missing coverage; the engineer challenges conclusions and approves the complete closure before it is recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: Oversight requires repeated visits to evidence stores and manual status reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Assessment IDs, test IDs and native project roll-ups can connect evidence to the agreed scope.
tasks.still_hard: Completed tests can be irrelevant or give false assurance.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge test adequacy and the significance of unresolved risks.

ambition.what: Review unresolved security-test coverage weekly during a change programme rather than only at its final assessment.

tasks.altitude: Less evidence chasing; oversight responsibility and assessors' execution work remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess whether tests cover realistic attack paths

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scope-linked assessment records and status roll-ups can reduce evidence chasing but cannot establish test adequacy.

assumptions: Boundary is the engineer's oversight, not assessor execution or system test runtime. Existing assessors produce evidence as part of their separate work; this design adds no new fields to their job. Shares are provisional.

Existing repositories supply assessment ID, test ID, target, run date, outcome, evidence location and owner. s1 supplies scope and criteria; s2 checks and manually maps absent identifiers. Missing or stale evidence remains visibly unresolved.
s3 saves repeated status comparison only; retained time checks missing coverage. s4 judges content and challenges assessors. Native project and assessment views are tested before custom connectors.
The closure is an oversight record, not automatic risk acceptance or permission to deploy. s6 approves its exact final text and unresolved conditions; changed evidence requires renewed review.
research_questions: Does a scope-linked view reveal missing tests without equating completed status with adequate evidence?

already_counted.description: Inspect coverage exceptions and approve final closure

incremental.description: Maintain scope mappings and stale-evidence checks

approvals.approved_version: Final oversight closure revision and unresolved conditions approved in s6; changed text or supporting evidence voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 12.5 gathering, nine status-reconciliation and five record-entry hours less two upkeep. Low assumes all evidence requires manual mapping and status checking, leaving final record entry only. Oversight judgement and assessor labour receive no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated security evidence and configuration handling while retaining risk and service judgements.
role.ambitious_version: Challenge unresolved security-test coverage more often with traceable evidence and unchanged accountability.
